timing: Specified after initial large-lesion pilot and before this dose/mean-replacement run
reason: Large lesions erase memory in both target and control groups; separate information removal from lost recurrent-drive amplitude
interventions: selected source activity replaced by (1-dose)*h + dose*independent calibration mean
class: all stored spatial-path predictive labels, including shift-window-edge units; legacy threshold classification
controls: 20 fixed non-PGC subsets matched in count, calibration mean activity, RMS activity, and outgoing recurrent-column norm
initialization: 40 valid motion-input steps followed by 200 zero-input steps; common initial state for every intervention
perturbation: initially orthogonal to two empirical position-translation tangents and state scaling; preserve nonnegative rates
metrics: projective state spread across initial positions
normal-perturbation pair separation relative to each intervention's own unperturbed trajectory
cautions: one trained network, no seed-level population inference
initial normal perturbations can later shear into phase directions
zero-input bias-free ReLU dynamics are homogeneous; do not assume a fixed-radius torus
activity normalization is used only for scoring, never to alter the network update
